learning_outcomes.text: Understand the design and structure of complex digital systems, interrelated with other disciplines, especially computer science and automation.
Understand and comprehend the different forms of representing quantities in binary.
Understand and comprehend asynchronous and synchronous sequential systems.
Understand and comprehend general application digital systems such as memories and PLDs (Programmable Logic Devices).
Understand and comprehend microprocessor systems, their applications, and interconnection with other devices.

syllabus_topics: Binary arithmetic: Adders, Subtractors, Arithmetic Logic Units (ALU), Multipliers, Dividers, Operations in BCD codes, Comparators.
Combinational logic blocks: Multiplexers and demultiplexers, Encoders and decoders, Shifters.
Methodology and basic tools for digital circuit design.
Hierarchical and modular design of an ALU.
Sequential logic blocks: Parallel input/output registers, Counters, Shift registers.
Design and simulation of an FSM-based sequential system.
Design, simulation, and implementation of a serial communication controller.
Memory logic blocks: RAM and ROM memories, Multiport memories, Register banks, Look-Up Tables (LUT), FIFO structures, LIFO structures.
Programmable Logic Devices: Programmable Logic Array (PLA), Complex Programmable Logic Device (CPLD), Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA).
Hardware platforms for emulation and rapid prototyping.
Design, simulation, and implementation of sequential systems with memory.
RISC processor structure: Data path, Control unit.
Design and simulation of a reduced single-cycle RISC-V processor.
Design and simulation of a reduced pipelined RISC-V processor.
Implementation and verification of a reduced RISC-V microcontroller.
teaching_methods: Personal study, individual or group work, and bibliography reading
assessment_rules: For continuous assessment, the final written exam contributes 60%, lab practices 25%, and a design project 15%. A minimum score of 4 out of 10 is required for the written exam and lab practices to apply the weighted average. If the minimums are not met, the final grade is capped at 3; if minimums are met but the written exam is failed, the final grade is capped at 5. The written exam and lab practices are recoverable in the extraordinary call, but the design project is not. For global assessment, a single final exam accounts for 75% and a lab exam for 25%, with a minimum of 4 in each required.
